traits.note: Watson and Dallwitz, The Families of Flowering Plants (DELTA data, items edited May 2026), family Portulacaceae, which takes in Talinaceae: leaves alternate or opposite; leaves simple; margins entire; veins pinnate or single; blades linear, lanceolate, oblanceolate, ovate or obovate; stipules usually present, rarely absent; plants hermaphrodite; ovary usually superior, rarely half inferior; floral cup present or absent; stems woody or herbaceous; flowers solitary or in cymes; flowers actinomorphic or zygomorphic; perianth sepals and petals or tepals; fruit capsule; stamens 3 to 50; carpels (2-) 3 (-9). Read from the coded states by script (spec-rework/b1/delta/mapdelta.py); a state the authors qualify (rarely, usually, a share) keeps its word, an unqualified one beside a usual state reads as sometimes.

traits.leaf_arrangement.note: German Wikipedia, 'Talinaceae' (read 2026-10-19 through the GBIF species API descriptions, dataset 'German Wikipedia - Species Pages', as de.wikipedia.org itself was blocked; lower trust; our translation): leaves alternate (wechselständig), often somewhat fleshy; FNA Talinum: alternate or subopposite; Flora of China Talinum: alternate or partly opposite.

traits.leaf_division.note: German Wikipedia, 'Talinaceae' (read 2026-10-19 through the GBIF species API descriptions, dataset 'German Wikipedia - Species Pages', as de.wikipedia.org itself was blocked; lower trust; our translation): simple blades.

traits.leaf_margin.note: Flora of North America vol. 4 (2003), Talinum (eFloras flora_id=1 taxon_id=132245, read 2026-10-19): margins entire (and the Portulacaceae family account: mostly entire).

traits.leaf_venation.note: Kept from the library family file (Watson and Dallwitz DELTA data): veins pinnate or single (Portulacaceae s.l.); not checked in the sources read.

traits.leaf_shape.note: Kept from the library family file (Watson and Dallwitz DELTA data): blades linear to obovate (Portulacaceae s.l.); German Wikipedia: blades very variable, sometimes asymmetric. Not narrowed.

traits.stipules.note: German Wikipedia, 'Talinum' (read 2026-10-19 through the GBIF species API descriptions, dataset 'German Wikipedia - Species Pages', as de.wikipedia.org itself was blocked; lower trust; our translation): true stipules absent, but small inconspicuous scales present that fall early (Talinaceae: two scales in the leaf axils). Flora of China Talinum: axils naked. FNA Portulacaceae: exstipulate except Portulaca and Talinopsis.

traits.sexual_system.note: German Wikipedia, 'Talinaceae' (read 2026-10-19 through the GBIF species API descriptions, dataset 'German Wikipedia - Species Pages', as de.wikipedia.org itself was blocked; lower trust; our translation): species can be dioecious, but mostly the flowers are bisexual.

traits.ovary_position.note: German Wikipedia, 'Talinaceae' (read 2026-10-19 through the GBIF species API descriptions, dataset 'German Wikipedia - Species Pages', as de.wikipedia.org itself was blocked; lower trust; our translation): three to five carpels united into a superior, one-chambered ovary; FNA Talinum: ovary superior.

traits.hypanthium.note: Kept from the library family file (Watson and Dallwitz DELTA data): floral cup present or absent (Portulacaceae s.l.); not checked.

traits.woodiness.note: German Wikipedia, 'Talinaceae' (read 2026-10-19 through the GBIF species API descriptions, dataset 'German Wikipedia - Species Pages', as de.wikipedia.org itself was blocked; lower trust; our translation): shrubs, some subshrubs, annual or perennial herbs, rarely small caudiciform trees; Talinella climbing shrubs. File kept.

traits.inflorescence.note: German Wikipedia, 'Talinum' (read 2026-10-19 through the GBIF species API descriptions, dataset 'German Wikipedia - Species Pages', as de.wikipedia.org itself was blocked; lower trust; our translation): flowers single in the leaf axils or several in terminal panicles; FNA Talinum: paniculate, racemose or cymose; Flora of China Talinum: a thyrse or panicle, very rarely solitary.

traits.flower_symmetry.note: German Wikipedia, 'Talinaceae' (read 2026-10-19 through the GBIF species API descriptions, dataset 'German Wikipedia - Species Pages', as de.wikipedia.org itself was blocked; lower trust; our translation): flowers radially symmetric (radiärsymmetrisch); also German Wikipedia 'Talinum'.

traits.perianth.note: German Wikipedia, 'Talinaceae' (read 2026-10-19 through the GBIF species API descriptions, dataset 'German Wikipedia - Species Pages', as de.wikipedia.org itself was blocked; lower trust; our translation): a double perianth: only two sepals, early-falling or kept into fruit, and two to five petals.

traits.flower_merosity.note: Flora of North America vol. 4 (2003), Talinum (eFloras flora_id=1 taxon_id=132245, read 2026-10-19): petals 5 or rarely more; Flora of China 5(-10); German Wikipedia Talinum usually five, rarely to seven.

traits.fruit_type.note: German Wikipedia, 'Talinaceae' (read 2026-10-19 through the GBIF species API descriptions, dataset 'German Wikipedia - Species Pages', as de.wikipedia.org itself was blocked; lower trust; our translation): fruit a berry or a loculicidal, many-seeded capsule; FNA and Flora of China Talinum: capsule 3-valved.

traits.stamens.note: German Wikipedia, 'Talinaceae' (read 2026-10-19 through the GBIF species API descriptions, dataset 'German Wikipedia - Species Pages', as de.wikipedia.org itself was blocked; lower trust; our translation): 15 to 35 stamens; Flora of China Talinum 5-30, German Wikipedia Talinum 10-30.

traits.carpels.note: German Wikipedia, 'Talinaceae' (read 2026-10-19 through the GBIF species API descriptions, dataset 'German Wikipedia - Species Pages', as de.wikipedia.org itself was blocked; lower trust; our translation): three to five carpels; FNA Talinum 3[-5].
